questions.q: Why is an `enum` generally safer than a plain `String` for representing a fixed set of options like Low/Medium/High?
options: An enum variable can only ever be assigned one of its declared values, so a typo is caught as a compile error rather than causing a silent runtime bug
Enums run faster than Strings in every comparison
Strings cannot be compared with == in Apex
Enums automatically translate their values into every supported language
questions.explain: Because an enum's possible values are fixed and checked at compile time, a typo like a misspelled value is caught before the code ever runs, unlike an arbitrary String.

questions.q: What does `when else` do inside a `switch on` statement?
options: It is required syntax even if every possible value is already handled
It repeats the switch statement in a loop
It provides a fallback branch that runs when none of the earlier `when` branches matched
It throws a compile error if reached
questions.explain: when else works like a default/ELSE branch, running only if none of the preceding when clauses matched the switched value.

questions.q: What is a wrapper class, fundamentally, in Apex?
options: A special built-in Apex type reserved for Lightning Web Components only
A class that can only contain static methods
A subclass that must extend Exception
An ordinary class whose purpose is to bundle several related values together for a specific calling context, such as an LWC method's return shape
questions.explain: A wrapper class is not a distinct language feature — it's a regular class used specifically to bundle related data together, often to match what a Visualforce page, LWC method, or REST response needs to return.

questions.q: In what sense are the Request/Result classes from Lesson 40's @InvocableMethod the same kind of thing as this lesson's OpportunitySummary class?
options: They are unrelated; one is an enum and the other is a wrapper class
Both are wrapper classes — the same general pattern of bundling related fields together, applied to Flow's input/output requirements instead of an LWC's data shape
Request/Result classes must always extend OpportunitySummary
They share no actual structural similarity
questions.explain: Both are ordinary classes used to bundle related fields for a specific calling context — Flow's required List-of-wrapper-class shape in one case, and an LWC-friendly data shape in the other.

questions.q: Can a `when` branch in a `switch on` statement match more than one value at once?
options: Yes, by separating multiple values with commas in the same when branch, e.g. `when LOW, MEDIUM { ... }`
No, each when branch can only match exactly one value
Only if the values are of different enum types
Only inside a trigger, never inside a regular class
questions.explain: A single when branch can list multiple comma-separated values that all route to the same branch of logic.
